## Overview

This model uses letter-sound knowledge ($L$) and phoneme blending ($B$) to describe the assigned-arm word-reading contrast. Unlike the parallel model [MED-066](../lrp-rli-med-066/), the blending leg also conditions on post-letter-sound score. The calculation integrates blending conditional on each simulated letter-sound value.

Both mediators and word reading use Beta-Binomial likelihoods in the randomised t1-to-t2 window. Every leg uses the same pre-exposure adjustment vector, including outcome and mediator baselines, baseline vocabulary and hearing, speech and memory terms. Read the saved plan for the fitted rows and active terms.

## Interpretation

- Compare the joint indirect component through $\{L, B\}$ with the parallel model's component. Agreement describes sensitivity to this modelling choice; it does not verify the assumed chain.
- The $L \to B$ coefficient is an adjusted same-wave association. It cannot establish that blending follows letter sounds in time or causally.
- Separate path components depend on mediator order and decomposition assumptions. Report them as exploratory components of the fitted model.

Latent ability and treatment-induced dose confounding prevent a causal interpretation of the decomposition. The shared assessment wave also limits temporal interpretation. See [the common-adjustment decision](../../../notes/202608231500-mediation-585-remediation.md) and [the mediation limits](../../../METHODS.md#2-bayesian-statistical-models).
